2608.29995.title: Generating Clinical Vignettes that Preserve Cognitive Formulations
2608.29995.paper_summary: Large language models can generate fluent clinical case vignettes, but fluency alone does not ensure fidelity to a specifiable clinical structure. We introduce FORMA, a theory-grounded framework that compiles a cognitive model of a disorder into a directed weighted graph, samples a person-specific configuration of that graph, and validates whether the generated vignette preserves the specified components and causal links. We instantiate FORMA on Posttraumatic Stress Disorder using the Ehlers and Clark cognitive model, generating 16,500 vignettes across 500 personas, 11 generation models, and three ablation conditions. Evaluation combines an external edge-recovery probe, two clinical experts, a scaled LLM judge, and a clinician user study with 100 licensed practitioners. The cognitive graph is recoverable from full-condition vignettes (MCC = +0.41, AUC = 0.70) but not from zero-shot generation (MCC = +0.01, AUC = 0.50). Experts rate full vignettes substantially higher than zero-shot alternatives, and clinicians perceive them to be human-written 85% of the time, compared with 22% for zero-shot. FORMA also reduces demographic disparity in perceived quality by 1.5-7x. These results show that cognitive formulation can serve as an auditable specification for scalable synthetic clinical text generation. A repository with the data and code is available online: https://github.com/Amit-Oren/FORMA.
2608.29995.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型可以生成流暢的臨床案例小品，但僅有流暢性並不能確保符合可指定的臨床結構。我們介紹了FORMA，一個基於理論的框架，將疾病的認知模型編譯成有向加權圖，並從該圖中抽樣出特定於個人的配置，然後驗證生成的小品是否保留了指定的組件和因果鏈。我們在創傷後壓力症上實現了FORMA，使用Ehlers和Clark的認知模型，生成了16,500個小品，涵蓋500個角色、11個生成模型和三個消融條件。評估結合了一個外部邊緣恢復探針、兩位臨床專家、一個擴展的LLM評審，以及一項包含100名持牌從業者的臨床用戶研究。從完整條件的小品中可以恢復認知圖（MCC = +0.41，AUC = 0.70），但從零樣本生成中則無法恢復（MCC = +0.01，AUC = 0.50）。專家對完整小品的評價顯著高於零樣本替代品，臨床醫生認為它們85%的時間是人類撰寫的，而零樣本則為22%。FORMA還將感知質量中的人口差異降低了1.5-7倍。這些結果表明，認知表述可以作為可審計的規範，用於可擴展的合成臨床文本生成。數據和代碼的存儲庫在線上可用：https://github.com/Amit-Oren/FORMA。
